explanation: Meiosis is a form of nuclear division that reduces the chromosome number in the daughter cells to half of that in the parent cell. It produces gametes, which are haploid (1n) reproductive cells (sperm and egg in humans), each carrying 23 chromosomes. Fertilization, which is the fusion of a sperm and egg, forms a diploid (2n) zygote with 46 chromosomes. Prior to dividing, meiotic cells undergo interphase (G1, S, and G2 phases). Meiosis involves two successive cell divisions: meiosis I and meiosis II. As a result, a single diploid (2n) cell divides to produce four haploid (1n) daughter cells, in contrast to mitosis which yields two diploid cells.
